artworks.title: Antigone
artworks.description: Leighton's solitary Antigone stands in classical drapery — the Theban sister as a Victorian icon of conscience, poised between burial and death. The canvas isolates Sophocles' heroine without Creon or corpse, pure resolve made flesh.

artworks.title: Oedipus and Antigone
artworks.description: Polish neoclassical canvas in the National Museum in Warsaw: the blind Oedipus leans on Antigone as she leads him into exile. Brodowski makes the sister the staff of Colonus — piety before the burial that will destroy her.

artworks.title: Antigone at the Bedside of Polynices
artworks.description: Benjamin-Constant's Antigone keeps vigil over Polynices' corpse — the sister who will sprinkle dust against Creon's decree. The painting stages the quiet moment before defiance becomes tragedy.

artworks.title: Ismene and Antigone Plead with Theseus
artworks.description: Abildgaard's canvas in the Statens Museum for Kunst shows Antigone and Ismene before Theseus, begging for their father's protection at Colonus. Danish neoclassicism turns Sophocles' last play into a scene of sisterly embassy.

artworks.title: Antigone Giving Burial to Polynices
artworks.description: Norblin's 1825 Prix de Rome painting (École des Beaux-Arts, Paris) shows Antigone burying Polynices against the city's ban. The handful of dust becomes the act that defines her — piety chosen over survival.

films.title: Antigone
films.description: Irene Papas' Antigone buries her brother against Creon's decree — Sophocles filmed in Greece, the sister who chooses the dead over the living law.

music.title: Antigone
music.description: Honegger's opera, after Cocteau's compression of Sophocles, sets Antigone's defiance in stark modern harmony — the burial as an act of music.

popCulture.title: Antigone
popCulture.creator: Sophocles
popCulture.description: Sophocles' sister who buries Polynices against Creon's decree — still the West's central drama of conscience versus the city's law.

popCulture.title: Antigone
popCulture.creator: Jean Anouilh
popCulture.description: Anouilh's Occupation-era rewrite makes Antigone a quiet refusal under tyranny — the Theban sister as a wartime allegory that never names its Vichy Creon.
